newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said that controversial graphics from the Commission working document competitiveness report would be available to journalists in his office but would not be included when transmitted to the Council.

In answer to a question spokesman Fillippo di Robilant said the Commission and the presidency had decided on Thursday to organise a mission to the Great Lakes area from Saturday night to Monday night. Di Robilant said destinations would be Kinshasa, Kigali, Gisenye and a visit to refugee camps.

Spokeswoman Sarah Lambert said Commissioner Neil Kinnock would attend a conference on fair and efficient transportation prices at the Centre Borschette. Lambert said the conference would start at 0900/0800 GMT, would then be split into workshops and would end with a news conference at 1700/1600 GMT.

Asked about the Commission's reaction to a railwaymen's march on 19 November in Brussels, Lambert said it was not the Commmission's intention to detroy rail but that despite huge social ramifications something had to be done to stop the rot.

Spokesman Patrick Child briefed on next Monday's ECOFIN Council. He said ministers would discuss Commission and European Monetary Institute reports on the state of convergence in the EU in 1996. He also said discussions would focus on the stability pact, in and pre-ins, future taxation system, legal statute of the euro and SEM 2000.

Spokesman Willy Helin said that Commissioner Karel Van Miert would meet Italian Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi on the fringe of the ECOFIN Council, shortly before lunchtime, to discuss reduction of Italian state holding Iri's debt.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/999: Agreement between the European Union and New-Zealand on sanitary measures affecting trade in live animals and animals products.
- Eurostat news release No 73/96: EU industrial production up 0.6%
